title: Pass the initializer, don’t call it

slides.say: Two little parentheses can make your component do expensive work on every single render.
React only uses the initial state once. But this line still calls create initial todos on every render, and throws the result away.
Pass the function itself, without calling it. Now React calls it only when the component is first created.

slides.text: An initializer must be pure, take no arguments, and return the initial state.
slides.say: This is called an initializer function. It should be pure, take no arguments, and return the starting value.

slides.text: Big array or slow calculation? Pass the function, not its result.
slides.say: The takeaway: when the starting value is costly to build, give use state the function, not its result.
